I've been working this land for 25 years in Quzhou, so I know what grows and what doesn't. My backbone is the wheat-maize rotation — that's 35 mu and I won't touch that system. It's reliable, the market is stable enough, and my well irrigation handles it fine. I'll plough deep before wheat as I always do — rotary tillage after harvest for maize since there's no time to waste between crops.

For wheat I'll use the improved variety I've been buying from the county seed station. I apply nitrogen in two shots — base and jointing stage. Three irrigations: winter, jointing, grain filling. Two pesticide runs, herbicide first then a fungicide pass near heading. Should get around 480 jin per mu.

Maize I always go hybrid,郑单958 or similar. One herbicide pass right after planting, then one spray for corn borers. Two irrigations are enough with normal summer rain, sometimes three if it's dry at tasseling.

For my other 30 mu, I grow vegetables and specialty crops for cash. Chili and watermelon are spring plantings. Stevia is steady — the contract buyer comes every year. Cabbage I plant in late summer for autumn harvest when prices usually recover after the summer glut. I use rotary tillage on all these plots since they're smaller and I don't need to go as deep.

I don't take risks with new varieties I haven't seen. I spray when I need to, not on a fixed schedule — but for cabbage caterpillars and chili anthracnose I know I'll need three to four passes minimum.
